## CONSENSUS
All outlets agree that the week's events represent an acceleration of the post-2024 geopolitical realignment. The tariff regime, WHO withdrawal, and regional military escalation are treated as connected symptoms rather than isolated incidents.

## FAULT LINES
The core ideological split is between those framing state retrenchment as necessary correction (Owner, Sovereign) and those reading it as systemic failure (Aspirant, Radical, Moralist). Hedonist sidesteps the political framing entirely.

## UNCOVERED ANGLES
Only the Moralist covered the humanitarian cost of the WHO funding gap in concrete terms — citing projected excess mortality figures that other outlets omitted entirely.

## WHAT TO WATCH
Watch how the Aspirant frames the next round of asylum policy announcements: the £40,000 scheme's three-month review is due in April, and the framing will reveal whether the political consensus has shifted.
